topics.title: A harvest poem: praise, personification and festivals

learn.hook: When fields turn gold, villages across India sing, dance and say thank you. A harvest poem joins that song.
points: 'Harvest Hymn' is a poem that celebrates the harvest and gives thanks to nature and to farmers' hard work.
A hymn is a song of praise. A harvest hymn praises the earth, rain and sun that help crops grow, and the people who grow them.
Personification gives human actions to non-human things: 'The golden fields bow low to greet the sun.' Fields cannot really bow, but the image shows heavy, ripe crops bending.
India celebrates harvest festivals in many regions: Pongal in Tamil Nadu, Lohri and Baisakhi in Punjab, Bihu in Assam, Onam in Kerala, and Makar Sankranti in many states.
Harvest poems often use warm, bright imagery (gold, glowing, ripe) and a joyful, grateful tone.

example.q: Read this original poem: 'Golden fields bow low to greet the sun, / The sickles sing: the reaping has begun! / Rain gave its silver, soil gave its might, / Now every grain glows warm and bright.' Think it through: find two examples of personification and say what the tone is.
steps: Fields 'bow low to greet the sun': bowing and greeting are human actions.
Sickles 'sing': singing is a human action, given to a tool.
Words like golden, glows, warm and bright, and the exclamation, sound happy.
Rain and soil are thanked for what they 'gave', so the poem is grateful too.
example.answer: Personification: the fields bow and greet; the sickles sing. The tone is joyful and grateful.

learn.reallife: At Pongal, families cook the new rice in milk until it boils over, and at Lohri people gather around a bonfire to celebrate the season. Harvest time is thanksgiving time.

games.title: About the harvest poem
items: In the poem, the fields 'bow low to greet the sun'.
That is the first line, an example of personification.
A hymn is a song of praise.
The poem says the sickles are crying.
The poem says the sickles sing.
The poem thanks the rain and the soil.
'Rain gave its silver, soil gave its might.'
Personification compares two things using 'like' or 'as'.
That is a simile. Personification gives human qualities to non-human things.
The tone of the poem is sad and angry.
Bright words and an exclamation give it a joyful tone.

quiz.q: Read: 'Golden fields bow low to greet the sun.' Which figure of speech is used?
quiz.explain: Fields are given the human actions of bowing and greeting.
quiz.mistake: Calls any poetic image a simile

quiz.explain: A hymn is a song of praise or thanks.

quiz.q: Read: 'The sickles sing: the reaping has begun!' What does 'reaping' mean?
quiz.explain: To reap is to cut and gather a crop. Sickles are the tools used for it.

quiz.q: Read: 'Rain gave its silver, soil gave its might.' What does 'silver' stand for here?
quiz.explain: The poet uses 'silver' to describe shining drops of rain that helped the crops.

quiz.q: Pongal is a harvest festival of which state?
quiz.explain: Pongal is celebrated in Tamil Nadu, when the new rice is cooked.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the regional harvest festivals

quiz.q: Which word best describes the tone of a harvest hymn?
quiz.explain: Harvest hymns give thanks, so the tone is grateful and joyful.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about the poem's feeling

quiz.q: Bihu, celebrated with dance and music, is a festival of which state?
quiz.mistake: Links 'Bihu' with 'Bihar' because the names look alike

quiz.q: Read the last two lines: 'Rain gave its silver, soil gave its might, / Now every grain glows warm and bright.' Which two words rhyme?
quiz.explain: 'Might' and 'bright' end with the same '-ight' sound.
quiz.mistake: Looks for repeated letters instead of end sounds

teach.ask: Gappu hears villagers singing in the golden fields. What is a harvest hymn, and why do people sing it?
teach.praise: La la la! A harvest hymn is a song of thanks to nature and farmers for the harvest. I want to sing too!
teach.nudge: What is the song saying to nature? What has just been gathered from the fields?

topics.title: Farmers and nature: crops, seasons and farm words

learn.hook: Rice loves the monsoon and wheat loves the winter. A farmer reads the seasons like a book!
points: Kharif crops are sown at the start of the monsoon (around June-July) and harvested around September-October: rice, maize, cotton, jowar, bajra.
Rabi crops are sown in winter (around October-November) and harvested in spring (around March-April): wheat, gram, mustard, barley, peas.

Farm work follows an order: ploughing (loosening the soil), sowing (planting seeds), irrigation (watering), weeding (removing unwanted plants), harvesting (cutting the crop), threshing (separating grain from stalks).
Collective nouns for farm and nature: a herd of cattle, a flock of birds, a swarm of locusts, a sheaf of wheat, a bunch of bananas.
Farmers depend on nature (rain, sunlight, healthy soil), so they care for it by saving water and keeping soil fertile.

example.q: Think it through: Ramesh sows seeds in June when the rains start, and harvests in October. Is his crop kharif or rabi, and which crop could it be: wheat or rice?
steps: Sown with the monsoon in June and harvested in October: that is the kharif season.
Rice is a kharif crop; wheat is a rabi crop.
So the crop is kharif, most likely rice.

learn.reallife: The roti you eat is usually made from wheat, a rabi crop, and the rice in your plate is usually a kharif crop.

games.title: From field to grain
games.prompt: Put the farming steps in order

quiz.q: Which of these is a rabi crop?
quiz.explain: Wheat is sown in winter and harvested in spring, so it is a rabi crop.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up kharif and rabi crops

quiz.q: Kharif crops are sown at the start of which season?
quiz.explain: Kharif crops need lots of water, so they are sown when the monsoon begins.
Threshing separates the grain from the harvested stalks.

quiz.q: Which step comes right after sowing?
quiz.explain: Seeds need water to grow, so irrigation comes after sowing.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the order of farm work

quiz.q: Choose the correct collective noun: 'a ___ of cattle'.
quiz.explain: A group of cattle is a herd. A flock is used for birds or sheep.
quiz.mistake: Uses a collective noun meant for other animals

quiz.q: Choose the correct collective noun: 'a ___ of wheat'.
quiz.explain: A bundle of cut wheat stalks tied together is a sheaf.
quiz.mistake: Picks a collective noun used for animals

quiz.q: Read: 'Ramesh sows seeds in June when the rains start, and harvests in October.' What type of crop is this?
quiz.explain: June sowing with the monsoon and October harvest is the kharif pattern.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the months in the sentence

quiz.explain: Irrigation means watering fields through canals, wells, pipes or sprinklers.

teach.ask: Gappu asks: Why do farmers grow rice in the rainy season and wheat in winter?
teach.praise: Peck peck! Rice is a kharif crop that needs monsoon rain, and wheat is a rabi crop that grows in winter. Farmers follow nature's seasons!
teach.nudge: Which crops need lots of rain? What are the two main crop seasons called?
